The code that makes the objects a report's content reads

Source: R/spec_parts.R
tfl_data_code.Rd

A table's content reads one object – the study's ARD (ard), or the records of a dataset (data, a table of records: table_plan(value = )) – and each part appended to it (plan_append()) its own: the ARD, or a dataset's records under the part's object name (adpc). This writes the code that makes each of them, as the report's program has it before the content's code (tfl_content_code()): a dataset's records as a listing's data part (tfl_listing_code() part = "data": read, the analysis set's subjects, the condition), the ARD as the study ARD's rows of the report. A statement two objects share (a dataset read once) is written once, with the first.

Usage

tfl_data_code(output, study, ard = TRUE)

Arguments

output

A report (tfl_output()) or its id.

study

The study (tfl_read_study_spec()), or its folder.

ard

FALSE leaves the ARD's code out (a program that writes its own: the study's ARD program, its rework).

Value

A named list, one element an object (data, ard, a part's object), each its lines of code.

Examples

o <- tfl_output("T-1", "table", content = list(
  tfl_item("table_plan", list(cols = "TRT01A"))))
st <- tfl_read_study_spec(system.file("extdata", "spec-yaml", package = "tflspec"))
tfl_data_code(o, st)
#> $ard
#> [1] "# the study ARD's rows of this report"                                    
#> [2] "ard <- readRDS(\"output/ard/ard.rds\") |>\n  subset(output_id == \"T-1\")"
#>
